# `plasma::D3D9Drawing`

[Game reference](../README.md) › [ui](../ui.md) › `plasma::D3D9Drawing`

- **Kind:** class
- **Status:** verified (source: kyubu)
- **Builds:** Cube.exe, Cube.exe only
- **C:** `plasma_D3D9Drawing` in `cubeworld/types.h`
- **Lua:** `cubeworld.cast("plasma_D3D9Drawing", address)`
- **Evidence:** `rtti:plasma::D3D9Drawing`, `probe:title-scene`
- **Confirmed by:** [title-scene](../probes.md#title-scene)

the Direct3D 9 drawing of one shape: its vertices and indices on the CPU and in buffers, its bounds, and the engine it draws with. A node's shape has one per fill and per stroke, which is why a node is drawn two times in a frame. Base plasma::Drawing; vtable 0x721548

| Offset | Name | Type | Status | Confirmed by | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0x110 | `bounds` | `float[4]` | verified |  | min x, min y, max x, max y of the shape's points, in the node's own units (before the engine's transform) |
| 0x124 | `engine` | [`plasma::D3D9Engine*`](plasma_D3D9Engine.md) | verified | [title-scene](../probes.md#title-scene) | the engine the drawing draws with; draw and updateBuffers reach the device, the shaders and the matrices through it |
| 0x128 | `vertex_buffer` | `void*` | candidate |  | IDirect3DVertexBuffer9*, 48 bytes a vertex (position 2 floats, 4 floats, 4 floats, 2 floats). Null until updateBuffers has run; draw does nothing when it is null |
| 0x12C | `index_buffer` | `void*` | candidate |  | IDirect3DIndexBuffer9*, 32-bit indices, drawn as a triangle list. Null for a shape with no indices (draw then draws nothing) |
